title: Hopeverse: Villain Wedding Theme v7 (hype and punch)
story: A stylish, suave villain makes his slow-motion entry at his own grand wedding.

brief.notes: Jithesh 29 Oct 11:30: 'no hype, no punch, no attention making in music score.' v7 = v6 with mass-entry hype: a huge attention hit in the first second, hard-hitting drums, a punch hit on every section change, drum-built tension before each drop, and a harder groove (half-time only in the glide). Handpan kept as the signature voice. Section times unchanged so the film cuts still land. LOCKED by Jithesh 29 Oct 13:37 ('Lock it'): take 2, mastered = films/villain-wedding-v4.mp3, the final villain wedding theme.

positive_global_styles: a hyped, punchy, swaggering mass-entry theme for a stylish villain at his own grand South Indian wedding: high energy, goosebump-raising, every hit lands like a punch, composed like a senior blockbuster film composer
hard-hitting swagger groove at about 96 BPM, heavy punchy drums with huge low-end hits, crowd-pleasing mass energy
a huge punch hit (full band stab, deep sub boom and a thavil crack together) on the first beat of every new section
a catchy whistled 5-note signature hook that becomes the main melody, in a minor scale with Carnatic gamakam slides
a handpan (steel hang drum) is a signature voice of the track: its warm, mysterious, bell-like tones play the hook and shimmer through the groove

balanced fusion: a real festive wedding band (nadaswaram, thavil, brass band) and real veena, mridangam and strings share the spotlight equally with fresh slick electronics (fat synth bass, crisp electronic drums, finger snaps)
a twangy veena riff played like a cool surf guitar, and a slick melodic bass line moving like a second melody
loud, clean, wide, glossy, very punchy mix with big transients

positive_local_styles: the very first sound, at second zero: one massive attention hit, a full brass and thavil stab with a deep sub boom, then instant silence
then only two sounds: a lone handpan plays the villain's 5-note hook, mysterious, and his whistle answers it, while a low thavil pulse slowly speeds up to build tension
transition: a punch hit, then a hard-hitting swagger beat slams in with a fat melodic bass under the handpan hook and sharp finger snaps
transition: a punch hit, the thavil crashes in loud, the wedding nadaswaram blasts the hook over a big brass band, all locked to the villain's groove, high energy
ends with a thavil roll building up, then one full beat of silence
dance-move hook: stop-time, four huge punching unison band stabs with sub booms on the hook rhythm, short silences between them, each stab a sharp dance pose, then the groove slams back in harder
dance-move hook: a heavy, punchy half-time strut, huge drums on two and four, the hook on twangy veena like a surf guitar, finger snaps and fat synth bass, swagger
surprise: a punch hit and the groove switches to fast double time, the energy jumps
the veena and the nadaswaram trade the hook, faster and faster, the handpan answers every phrase
violins enter with a brand-new counter-hook on top, a drum build rises into the next section
the ketti melam: a frenzied, very loud wedding drum roll on thavil with huge hits
call and response: the full brass section shouts the hook, the thavil answers with punches
the key lifts up a whole step for the biggest, most hyped hook of the track
ends with a sudden stop: one bar of only the handpan and the whistle playing the hook
a massive punch hit and the full band slams the hook at full power, every instrument together, real and electronic, maximum hype
one final massive chord with a deep sub drop, a lighter snap, then silence
